subject: standard mixed model with matrix input

messages.author: 962d5fe16bb7c407
messages.subject: standard mixed model with matrix input
parts:
Dear Håvard /inla-ers

 

Could you point me how I can do the matrix version of the standard mixed model in INLA:

Y = X beta + Zb+ e

with X and Z matrices with real numbers, beta fixed normal prior, b~N(0,t1*Q) with Q a given precision matrix and t1 to be estimated and e~N(0,t2*R) with R given precision.

 

I would be  already very glad with r-inla code for R = I and X specified by a formula. So the real question is

 

Y = Zb+ e

with Z a matrix with real numbers, b~N(0,t1*Q) with Q a given precision matrix and t1 to be estimated and e~N(0,t2*I) and t2 to be estimated

 

I would use it for ridge regression and for P-splines. Yes, I know it can be done in INLA using the high rank approach, but we would like to explore alternatives, also for computational reasons.

 

Best wishes Cajo

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] standard mixed model with matrix input
parts:
Hi

There is currently no way of defining the Zb term directly, but you have
to do this using the A-matrix; see

http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools#TOC-Models-where-the-response-data-depends-on-linear-combinations-of-the-linear-predictor-

however, I see the point of adding this model... I'll put it on the
list.

Best
H

parts: I found a little snack in runme.r. It currently supposes implicitly that the fixed effects in the mixed model sum to zero!  This is shown in runme2, with the trivial correction in f(, constr = FALSE). In the plot the triangle are with constr = FALSE.  Cajo ter Braak
